problem.paragraph: A curve has equation $$y = f(x)$$ .

list.item: Write an expression for the slope of the secant line through the points $$P\left( {3,f(3)} \right)$$ and $$Q\left( {x,f(x)} \right)$$ .

problem.paragraph: A cliff diver plunges from a height of $$100$$ ft above the water surface. The distance the diver falls in $$t$$ seconds is given by the function $$d(t) = 16t^{2}{ft}$$ .

list.item: a.After how many seconds will the diver hit the water?
b.With what velocity does the diver hit the water?

problem.paragraph: If a rock is thrown upward on the planet Mars with a velocity of $$10m \slash s$$ , its height (in meters) after $$t$$ seconds is given by $$H = 10t - 1.86t^{2}$$ .

list.item: Find the velocity of the rock after one second.
Find the velocity of the rock when $$t = a$$ .
When will the rock hit the surface?
With what velocity will the rock hit the surface?

problem.paragraph: The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by the equation of motion $$s = 1 \slash t^{2}$$ , where $$t$$ is measured in seconds. Find the velocity of the particle at times $$t = a$$ , $$t = 1$$ , $$t = 2$$ , and $$t = 3$$ .
The displacement (in feet) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $$s = \frac{1}{2}t^{2} - 6t + 23$$ , where $$t$$ is measured in seconds.

list.item: Find the average velocity over each time interval: $$\left\lbrack {4,8} \right\rbrack$$ $$\left\lbrack {6,8} \right\rbrack$$ $$\left\lbrack {8,10} \right\rbrack$$ $$\left\lbrack {8,12} \right\rbrack$$
Find the instantaneous velocity when $$t = 8$$ .

Draw the graph of $$s$$ as a function of $$t$$ and draw the secant lines whose slopes are the average velocities in part (a). Then draw the tangent line whose slope is the instantaneous velocity in part (b).

a.A particle starts by moving to the right along a horizontal line; the graph of its position function is shown in the figure. When is the particle moving to the right? Moving to the left? Standing still?
b.Draw a graph of the velocity function.

Details A function is graphed on a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t (seconds) and is displayed from 0 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The vertical axis is labeled s (meters) and is displayed from 0 to 5 in increments of 1 unit. The function begins at (0, 0), goes linearly upward to the right until the point (1, 3), then runs horizontally rightward until (2, 3). It then goes linearly downward to the right to (3, 1), then runs horizontally rightward until (4, 1), and then goes linearly upward to the right to the point (6, 3).

solution.paragraph: Right: $$0 < t < 1$$ and $$4 < t < 6$$ ; left: $$2 < t < 3$$ ; standing still: $$1 < t < 2$$ and $$3 < t < 4$$

problem.paragraph: Symmetric Difference Quotient In Example 8 we approximated an instantaneous rate of change by averaging two average rates of change. An alternative method is to use a single average rate of change over an interval centered at the desired value. We define the symmetric difference quotient of a function $$f$$ at $$x = a$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {a - d,a + d} \right\rbrack$$ as
$$\frac{f(a + d) - f(a - d)}{(a + d) - (a - d)} = \frac{f(a + d) - f(a - d)}{2d}$$

list.item: Compute the symmetric difference quotient for the function $$D$$ in Example 8 on the interval $$\left\lbrack {2004,2012} \right\rbrack$$ and verify that your result agrees with the estimate for $$D^{\prime}(2008)$$ computed in the example.

Show that the symmetric difference quotient of a function $$f$$ at $$x = a$$ is equivalent to averaging the average rates of change of $$f$$ over the intervals $$\left\lbrack {a - d,a} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\left\lbrack {a,a + d} \right\rbrack$$ .

Use a symmetric difference quotient to estimate $$f^{\prime}(1)$$ for $$f(x) = x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 2$$ with $$d = 0.4$$ . Draw a graph of $$f$$ along with secant lines corresponding to average rates of change over the intervals $$\left\lbrack {1 - d,1} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\left\lbrack {1,1 + d} \right\rbrack$$ , and $$\left\lbrack {1 - d,1 + d} \right\rbrack$$ . Which of these secant lines appears to have slope closest to that of the tangent line at $$x = 1$$ ?
